observations.text: SP, due to a briefing method that treated CRM as a separate subject instead of integrating it into the navigation briefing, did not cover the CRM items of mission planning, communication and airmanship for the planned route. The division of duties between the cockpits for map reading, GPS handling and lookout was left unstated, and airborne the SP could not re-establish the leg sequence without assistance. The IP directed the actions at each turning point and executed part of the navigation task. The CRM box was checked only after the IP built the debriefing points on the SP's behalf.

SP, due to inadequate crew coordination between front and rear cockpit, did not use the CRM concept when the planned route had to be amended for weather and left the position and fuel state unverbalized to the IP. The SP did not reach the required course of action without assistance, with the result that the IP allocated the roles and executed part of the reroute. During the debriefing the areas for CRM development were identified by the IP and not by the SP.

SP integrated CRM into the navigation briefing and the debriefing at the level expected for the Training Section; however, the IFG/CRM matrix chart was used to highlight the particular items only after the IP's verbal prompts, on two occasions. Communication of the position relative to the next turning point was passed to the front cockpit with delay each time it was required. Marginal performance for the Training Section - independent use of the CRM matrix chart, without prompting, is expected to improve.

SP integrated CRM into the navigation briefing and the debriefing without the IP's prompting, using the IFG/CRM matrix chart to highlight the mission planning, communication and airmanship items of the route. Minor omissions in verbalizing the position and the next heading during the enroute phase were recognized and corrected by the SP in a timely manner, without the IP's intervention. The CRM concept was used when planning the low level legs and the debriefing points were raised by the SP. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP applied the CRM concept accurately and without delay in the navigation briefing, throughout the route and in the debriefing, and used the IFG/CRM matrix chart to highlight the mission planning, communication and airmanship items. The division of duties between the cockpits was stated before each leg and every deviation from the planned track and timing was communicated as it was recognized, without the IP's intervention. The areas for CRM development were raised on the SP's own initiative during the debriefing. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP demonstrated CRM performance above the desired level for the Training Section, integrating the CRM items into the navigation briefing and the debriefing in a standardized manner and using the IFG/CRM matrix chart without any prompting. When the route had to be amended for traffic and weather, the SP stated the role allocation, requested the information needed from the front cockpit in plain language and analyzed the situation through the CRM concept before selecting the new leg. Coordination deviations across the sortie were negligible, and in the debriefing the SP set the areas for CRM development and solicited comments on where CRM enhanced mission effectiveness and flight safety. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to mission planning carried out without any CRM structure, did not brief the division of duties, the communication plan or the airmanship items for the planned navigation profile. Airborne the intentions of the two cockpits were never consolidated and the SP did not complete the route without assistance, with the result that the IP directed the turn at each turning point and executed part of the recovery to the field. The CRM box was checked only after the IP conducted the debriefing points on the SP's behalf.

SP, due to ambiguity over who was flying and who was working the navigation task, did not confirm the allocation of duties when the aircraft was repositioned onto the next leg. The situation was not analyzed through the CRM concept and entries to the GPS were attempted from both cockpits at the same time. The SP did not regain the planned track without assistance, with the result that the IP reselected the active leg and flew part of the correction. In the debriefing the coordination breakdown was described by the IP and not by the SP.

SP, due to a briefing flow that omitted the IFG/CRM matrix chart, did not highlight the mission planning, communication and airmanship items applicable to the navigation sortie. Airborne the position, the fuel state and the intended next action were passed to the front cockpit only after the IP asked for them, on three occasions. The required calls at the turning points were made with delay and the debriefing points were raised only after the IP's verbal prompts.

SP, due to workload distribution that left the SP flying, reading the map and transmitting at the same time, did not maintain the communication element of CRM during the enroute legs. The picture between the cockpits was consolidated only after the IP prompted verbally for a position and fuel state report. Recognition of the coordination lapse came with delay, and the areas for CRM improvement were reached in the debriefing only under the IP's guidance.

SP integrated the CRM items into the navigation briefing, the flight and the debriefing within the standards of the Training Section; however, communication of the position twice lagged the actual passage of the turning point before the SP corrected it without the IP's intervention. The IFG/CRM matrix chart was used, but the airmanship subcategories were highlighted in less depth than the mission planning and communication items. Marginal performance for the Training Section - consistency in verbalizing the position at the moment of passing the turning point is expected to improve.

SP applied the CRM concept accurately and without delay when planning the route and when analyzing the in-flight change to the recovery, using the IFG/CRM matrix chart to highlight the mission planning, communication and airmanship items. Role assignment between the cockpits was stated before each leg and every deviation from the planned track and timing was verbalized without the IP's intervention. In the debriefing the SP identified the point at which CRM enhanced mission effectiveness and flight safety and proposed the areas for CRM development. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP demonstrated CRM performance above the desired level for the Training Section, integrating the CRM items into the navigation briefing and the debriefing in a standardized manner and using the IFG/CRM matrix chart without prompting. Under the increased workload of the low level legs the SP assigned the roles explicitly, requested the required information from the front cockpit in plain language and worked the navigation problem as a crew rather than individually. Coordination deviations across the sortie were negligible and in the debriefing the SP solicited comments on where CRM enhanced mission effectiveness and flight safety. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to a mission planning phase conducted without the CRM structure required for the navigation profile, did not brief the division of duties, the communication plan or the airmanship items. Airborne the two cockpits worked from different assumptions about the next turning point and the SP did not complete the route without assistance. The IP directed the turns and executed part of the recovery, and the debriefing points were built by the IP and not by the SP.

SP, due to an unshared assessment of the aircraft position between front and rear cockpit, did not provide the plain-language cross-talk needed to keep the navigation picture consolidated after the track diverged from the plotted route. The situation was not analyzed through the CRM concept and the SP did not re-establish the planned track without assistance. The IP took over the navigation task and flew part of the correction back to the route, and the CRM box was checked only after the IP led the debriefing.

SP, due to a debriefing method that reviewed the legs of the route without reference to the IFG/CRM matrix chart, did not highlight the mission planning, communication and airmanship items of the sortie. Airborne the required calls at the turning points were passed only after the IP's verbal prompts and the coordination lapse was recognized with delay. The areas for CRM development were reached only after the IP directed the discussion toward them.

SP, due to absent inquiry when the ground features observed did not match the expected picture on the map, did not question the shared plan with the front cockpit and did not use the CRM concept while analyzing the developing navigation error. The discrepancy was raised only after the IP prompted verbally and the track was corrected with delay. In the debriefing the SP described the communication breakdown only once the IP had structured the point.

SP, due to a briefing sequence that covered the communication plan after the route description instead of together with it, did not tie the required calls to the specific turning points of the profile. During the enroute phase two calls were passed late relative to the briefed points, and the SP recognized the mismatch and re-established the briefed communication flow without the IP's intervention. The CRM items were reviewed in the debriefing using the IFG/CRM matrix chart.

SP, due to task sequencing that concentrated the map, GPS and radio workload inside the turn at the turning point, did not verbalize the position and the new heading to the front cockpit as the leg changed. The omission was recognized by the SP shortly afterwards and the information was passed without the IP's intervention, so that the shared navigation picture between the cockpits was restored. Minor coordination errors of this type occurred twice and were self-corrected in a timely manner.

SP applied the CRM concept in the navigation briefing, throughout the route and in the debriefing with the accuracy and the speed expected for the Training Section; however, the airmanship subcategories were highlighted on the IFG/CRM matrix chart only after a short pause on each occasion. Communication with the front cockpit was correct in content, with the position report at each turning point made just inside the briefed timing. Marginal performance for the Training Section - a faster and more automatic use of the CRM matrix chart is expected to improve.

SP demonstrated CRM performance above the desired level for the Training Section, with the CRM items of mission planning, communication and airmanship integrated into the navigation briefing and the debriefing in a standardized manner. Throughout the route the role assignment was stated before every leg, the position and fuel state were verbalized at each turning point and the SP used the IFG/CRM matrix chart to close the points carried forward from the previous debriefing. Coordination deviations were negligible and the SP identified, without any prompting, the phase in which CRM enhanced mission effectiveness and flight safety. Above end of block MIF achieved.
